title: Before rebalancing: five checks
objectives: Explain why no written target means no rebalance yet.
body_md:
Rebalancing only makes sense against a target the client has agreed to. Check five things first.

| Check | Question | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Target mix | Is there a written target for each goal? | No target means nothing to rebalance to; set one first (Module 13) |
| Whole portfolio | Have we counted EPF, PPF, FDs and holdings elsewhere? | Drift is measured on the total, not just the funds we manage |
| Drift size | How far is each asset class from target, in percentage points? | Small drifts aren't worth the cost of acting |
| Costs | Will selling trigger exit loads or short-term gains? | Costs can outweigh the benefit of a small rebalance |
| Client situation | Any goal near, or change in income or risk profile? | That may call for a new target, not a rebalance |
example: No written target? Set one first (Module 13) — there is nothing to rebalance to.
say: No target means nothing to rebalance to; set one first.
Drift is measured on the total, not just the funds we manage.
never: Ignore holdings outside the funds we manage.
